notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/merchantprofile.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/merchantprofile.md at 4c69058 (“docs: add Merchant Profile guide”). The guide's Sources note says “Checked 28 October 2026” on 0.1.78, the 27 October build of Biscuit's main; the evidence records the same check (28 October 2026, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02, Biscuit's main at dbe0e02), so items citing the note or the evidence carry checkedOn 2026-10-28 and checkedVersion 0.1.78-dbe0e02, and none is flagged as stale. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October), the build the guide was checked on; npm run coin:status now shows one newer upstream commit (9a999cd, 28 October), not installed. Installed MerchantProfile.tsx and Avatar.tsx match every guide and evidence sentence used here, read from source, not run (token values through the package's own resolver): title and subtitle default to Uber's sample name and UPI ID; the root is a View, a centred column with 16 px side padding, a 12 px gap and no width, with accessibilityRole header and accessibilityLabel undefined (the label the source builds from the title and subtitle is never used); the avatar is an Avatar with style Image, given the profile's modes and then avatarProps spread over them, so avatarProps.modes replaces the profile's modes; with no imageSource the Avatar shows its bundled photo; Avatar Size resolves L 42 (the default), M 36, S 29, XS 14; the name is 16 px bold on a 20 px line (the token's 18 raised to 1.2 × 16, rounded up), the UPI ID 12 px medium on 16; both lines are always rendered, centred, with no line limit, so they wrap, and an empty one keeps its gap; all 12 merchantProfile tokens resolve the same in Light and Dark. No guide or evidence sentence disagrees with the installed source. One thing reads wider than the guide, from the source, not run: avatarProps is spread onto the Avatar whole, so an onPress in it would make the avatar alone pressable; “it doesn’t press” holds for the profile as the guide uses it, and no rule here mentions avatar presses. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every profile, its VStack columns and the In context components) and no Avatar Size (the guide's Avatar Size M card shows the option; no guide sentence says some content needs it). The In context example is the Merchant Profile alone: the guide's payment screen puts it in a VStack (Slot gap XL, stretched) with an AmountInput holding a MoneyValue and a NoteInput (each set to Context3 Amount Input) and a Pay ₹1,200 Button. AmountInput, NoteInput and MoneyValue have no entry in this pack, and unlike IconCapsule in ActionTile's icon slot they are not parts of the Merchant Profile but the screen's own, so under “Use only components with an entry” they are left out; a VStack with only the profile and the Pay button would show a payment with no amount, so the example does not add one, and its purpose says what the screen lays out. The guide's logo is a docs asset (jio-gold-logo.png); as in the ProfileCard entry, the examples pass a { uri } that stands for the merchant's own logo (the package's JSDoc example passes a string URL, which the Avatar also accepts). Copy is the guide's own (Jio Gold, UPI ID: jiogold@jio, Amazon Pay, UPI ID: amazonpay@apl, AP, Uber India Systems Private Limited). Left out of examples (three at most): the playground, the Avatar Size M card, the Long name and Long UPI ID cards (the state covers them), the Registered name and Labelled ID cards (their copy is in content good), the In context readout (“Paying Jio Gold, UPI ID jiogold@jio”, a documentation line) and the Don'ts. Not recorded: style (the building rules keep style off Coin components); the evidence's colours; the mode collections the facts list other than Avatar Size (Badge Size, context 10, Context2, Context4, Page type, Profile Card Appearance), which no guide sentence covers and the evidence's Limits keep out of the guide; Biscuit's MerchantProfile.mdx (its uses, its “wrap in a Pressable”, which the guide's Limits rule out, its default-label and theming claims, and its 'Avatar Size': 'XL', which does not exist); the Storybook story list and its stock-photo stories; Figma's hard line break in its sample name. Per the pack's rules the dead accessibilityLabel is not a gap (a missing screen-reader name); the guide states it, so it is an accessibility rule and an evidence fact. The heading root is a gap, as #423 lists it. Gaps name Component Bug #423 as the evidence does, without a board status. Content bad is empty: the Don'ts show configurations (no avatarProps, subtitle left out), not wording. The Sources note renders whole: no line has a missing value. Sorting (batch 7): the cross-check found three items to fix. The heading report was an accessibility rule marked recommended; it is a defect, kept only as a gap (#423). The Monogram rule took the example caption’s “two letters”; it now quotes the Configuration sentence (“their initials”). The In context example’s purpose no longer names AmountInput, MoneyValue and NoteInput (the guide’s source builds the screen with them, but they have no entry and the rendered guide does not name them).

examples.purpose: A payment screen opens with the merchant, the guide’s In context: Jio Gold’s logo, registered name, and UPI ID, so people know who they’re paying before they enter the amount. The screen lays out the rest (in the guide, the amount, a note and a Pay ₹1,200 button) and sends the payment. The URI stands for the merchant’s own logo.

<MerchantProfile
  title="Jio Gold"
  subtitle="UPI ID: jiogold@jio"
  avatarProps={{ imageSource: { uri: 'https://example.com/jio-gold-logo.png' } }}
/>
